correctness.rationale: The universal upper bound \(S(E)\le\sqrt3\) follows from Cauchy--Schwarz, Plancherel, and \(L^2\le L^\infty\). Equality forces equal coefficient moduli and constant Fourier modulus. Fourier uniqueness then requires cancellation at every nonzero directed difference. For a normalized support \(\{0,a,b\}\), repeating the difference \(a\) forces either an arithmetic-progression branch or an involution branch. Repeating all differences leaves exactly order-three progressions, order-four progressions, and Klein-four triples. Explicit unimodular coefficients make the first two flat, while the Klein-four equations force \(p,q\in\{\pm i\}\) and simultaneously \(\operatorname{Re}(p\overline q)=0\), an impossibility. The finite verifier only corroborates this algebraic proof.

value.rationale: The maximal Sidon value \(\sqrt{|E|}\) is the canonical extremal boundary, and three points are the first support size where nontrivial torsion geometry appears. The theorem gives a complete arbitrary-abelian-group classification, explains the exceptional \(N=4\) endpoint of the consecutive cyclic family, identifies the independent order-three branch, and isolates exactly why Klein-four geometry fails. This is a natural structural classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
